title: Children's Bedtime Stories — Episodic (Ages 3–4)
summary: Original sequential, single-narrator bedtime adventures for ages 3–4, primarily age three. Season one explores Willow Bend and completes the Little-Light Walk; season two travels west to Far Meadow, meets Lila, and completes a ribbon picnic. Season three travels east past Round Pond into Reed Meadow, meets Rill and Aunt Cress, and finishes Bo’s Book of Little Sounds. Places, relationships and objects persist between episodes; every night closes gently. Non-spoken caregiver explanations and citations do not assert developmental or sleep effects.
assumed_background: Age 3–4; prior episodes enrich continuity but each episode includes enough context to enjoy on its own.
series_title: Willow Bend and the Little Lights

lectures.title: Tess and the Map with Room for More
lectures.description: Tess begins a yellow map of Willow Bend and learns how many small places can fit into one familiar day.

lectures.title: Bo and the Humming Bridge
lectures.description: Bo listens to different footsteps and reeds on Pebble Bridge, while a violet pouch hints at someone farther along the path.

lectures.title: A Small Hello at Round Pond
lectures.description: Tess and Bo meet Nori, a careful observer of ripples, and find that friendship can begin with a quiet shared moment.

lectures.title: The Apple That Went Traveling
lectures.description: An especially round apple takes a rolling trip through the orchard and turns into a shared joke and a new mark on the map.

lectures.title: The Lantern That Leaned
lectures.description: Bo experiments with an orange paper lantern that leans to one side and discovers its tilt can become part of its charm.

lectures.title: The Little-Light Walk
lectures.description: The friends follow their mapped path through Willow Bend, recall the places they know, and watch the valley lights together.

lectures.title: The Other Side of Bell Hill
lectures.description: Tess, Bo, and Nori cross Bell Hill with Grandma Fern, discover Far Meadow, and meet Lila, whose blue-ribboned hat likes the wind.

lectures.title: Bo's Very Big Pocket
lectures.description: Bo stuffs a coat pocket with ordinary treasures and opens a very silly temporary museum on Far Meadow's Sitting Stone.

lectures.title: Nori and the Soft-Grass Path
lectures.description: Lila shows the friends a sheltered clover nook behind the Windbreak Tree; Nori helps choose how the newly discovered place appears on the map.

lectures.title: The Shadow with a Very Long Scarf
lectures.description: Lila visits Willow Bend, sees the Story House and lantern, and the friends notice their shadows looking different as the day passes.

lectures.title: The Ribbon That Wouldn't Sit Still
lectures.description: Friends gather in the Story House to arrange an orange, blue, and violet banner while the breeze gives their decorations ideas of its own.

lectures.title: The Picnic Beyond the Hill
lectures.description: The friends share a breezy picnic beneath the Windbreak Tree and recognize the places and friendships that now belong on Tess's expanding map.

lectures.title: The Path Past Round Pond
lectures.description: Nori leads the friends east of Round Pond to Reed Meadow, and Bo starts a blue notebook of little sounds.

lectures.title: Bo's Very Serious Listening Hat
lectures.description: Bo makes a paper listening hat, discovers that it mostly crinkles, and fills a second notebook page with bridge sounds.

lectures.title: The Croak Behind the Grass
lectures.description: A rounded bup leads the friends to Rill, a young frog in yellow boots, and a new friendship begins at Reed Meadow.

lectures.title: Lila and the Two Kinds of Wind
lectures.description: Lila travels east with Aunt Mallow, meets Rill, and helps fill the sound book with the different rustles of two meadows.

lectures.title: The Plink Under the Eaves
lectures.description: From a dry Story House, the friends trace a rainy plink to drops hitting a watering can and add its picture to their book.

lectures.title: The Last Little Sound
lectures.description: Friends from both sides of the valley read Bo’s five pages at Story House, discover a final paper sound, and shelve the completed book.
